A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
FM spectroscopy is a viable technique for obtaining high resolution spectra of weakly absorbing species.
we have developed a technique for the measurement of the fourth-overtone transition of HF, which can detect 10−6 molar concentrations of HF with a 25.6-cm absorption path length.
the FM technique is capable of detecting a single absorption event in the HF fourth overtome with an accuracy of ±0.0001 cm−1.
The main takeaway from our work is that
FM spectroscopy can be used to measure the broadening of a transition in an absorbing medium, even when that medium has a very small absorption coefficient.

the FM technique can provide a sensitivity that is comparable with or even better than that of a cw dye laser, but with the added advantages of a shorter time to obtain the data and a much higher resolution.
frequency modulated spectroscopy is a viable technique for the study of the fourth overtones of weakly absorbing diatomic molecules in the near infrared.
